title: Editorial: All about Epstein money - NewsBreak
text:
By THE BLADE EDITORIAL BOARD ,
2 hours ago
Follow the money!
The first rule of scandal investigation has been conspicuously ignored by the Department of Justice and Republican Congressional Committees in the Jeffrey Epstein sex trafficking case.
There’s been uproar around the Epstein case since Attorney General Pam Bondi said the DOJ had no evidence Epstein blackmailed any of the wealthy men who flew on his jet and attended parties at his homes around the world most notable for the underage girls he paid to be there.
AG Bondi said there was no client list in the Epstein case file, despite campaigning alongside the President and FBI officials saying there was a client list that would be released when Donald Trump was elected.
Read more Blade editorials
Now the House Oversight Committee is taking up the case with more partisan political theater. Boxes of documents from the DOJ Epstein file were delivered to the committee last week and subpoenas to Democratic notables, Bill and Hillary Clinton, former AG Merrick Garland, and former FBI Directors James Comey and Robert Mueller.
Somehow, the DOJ and House Oversight have neglected to seek the Treasury Department documents that show 4,725 Epstein financial transactions totaling nearly $1.1 billion, involving major U.S. banks and banks in Russia, Turkey, Belarus, and Turkmenistan. The movement of money from the United States to these foreign banks correlates to movement of young women from these nations to Epstein directed locations.
U.S. Senate Finance Committee member Ron Wyden (D., Ore.), a former chairman of the committee, spent three years digging up records at the Treasury Department and tried to no avail to get Republicans to go along with hearings on probable misuse of the banking system to facilitate Epstein’s sex trafficking.
Congress and the Justice Department have a duty to investigate why J.P. Morgan Chase, Bank of America, and Deutsche Bank failed to file required suspicious activity reports until Epstein was jailed in 2019.
Remember, Jeffrey Epstein was convicted on prostitution charges involving underage girls in Florida in 2008. The federal sex trafficking of minors charge came more than a decade later after moving a billion dollars worldwide with no questions asked.
The banking records show multi-million-dollar disbursements to Epstein accounts from dozens of ultra-wealthy men but there has been no DOJ or Congressional probe simply asking these men to explain why they sent Epstein so much money.
No serious investigation would skip that obvious step.
Just as important as a list of Epstein clients is an accounting of how a convicted sex criminal was able to move a billion dollars around the world through major U.S. banks without raising any red flags.
Epstein exposed systemic failure across the financial and the legal system that demands a no-holds-barred bipartisan investigation.
